answer: In an agent marketplace trading marble, basalt, and pigment, each seller identity must lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding, and the protocol limits each bonded identity to one active job. Creating more names grants no extra capacity unless each name posts its own bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds for a month, paying the capital cost even if the identities never win work.
